explanation: La bise (cheek-kissing) is the standard social greeting among friends, family, and acquaintances across France — it's not used for first business introductions, where a handshake is the norm instead. The tricky part is the number of kisses: most of the country does two, but some regions do one, three, or four, so it's best to follow the other person's lead.
local_tip: Start with the right cheek and let the other person set the pace and count — two kisses is the safest default if you're unsure.
regional_note: Crowdsourced regional surveys (such as the 'Combien de bises' poll) map real variation: two kisses is standard across most of France, three is common in parts of the Occitanie/Auvergne area, four persists among older residents in parts of eastern Brittany, and Brittany's Finistère region is one of the few areas where a single kiss is the norm.

also_check.note: Physical greetings like cheek-kissing aren't customary; a bow is the norm, though this is a difference in custom rather than an offense.
Cheek-kissing is also common as a greeting, though the number of kisses and which cheek to start with varies by region.
Cheek-kissing is generally reserved for close friends and family; a handshake is the safer default for acquaintances and business contacts.
